statements.quote: This pre-registered study directly compares human-human and human-AI collaboration dynamics across two creative tasks: the Alternative Uses Task (AUT) and creative short story writing.

This study was pre-registered on the Open Science Framework (OSF), including the experimental protocol, primary hypotheses, sample size determination, and planned analytical approach. The preregistration document can be accessed at https://osf.io/tveaf.
statements.locator: PDF p. 3, Methods, preregistration paragraph; markdown line 53

statements.quote: Any deviations or exploratory analysis not on the registry are noted in the relevant sections or detailed in the supplementary information.
statements.locator: PDF p. 4, Methods, continuation of preregistration paragraph; markdown line 55

statements.quote: The experiment was administered on Qualtrics, while the collaborative tasks were hosted on a custom external website. The matching of human participants was performed using the SMARTRIQS platform, a free, open-source tool for interactive Qualtrics experiments involving communication between multiple human participants or chatbots (Molnar, 2019).
statements.locator: PDF p. 4, Materials and Procedure, study platform and open-source software; markdown line 63

statements.quote: The study used prompt engineering to engage ChatGPT-4o as a creativity collaborator in the human-AI condition, tasking the model with generating original ideas for both the Alternative Uses Task (AUT) and creative short story writing. This means prompts were carefully designed with explicit constraints and instructions, so that it served as a creative and useful collaborator in the relevant tasks. The model was accessed via the OpenAI API through PythonAnywhere, by hosting a custom chat interface that was designed to visually match the human partner condition (see Fig. 1).
statements.locator: PDF p. 4, Materials and Procedure, ChatGPT-4o, prompts and custom interface; markdown line 67

statements.quote: Originality of AUT responses was assessed using Cross-Lingual Alternate Uses Scoring (CLAUS), a transformer model fine-tuned to match human ratings, hosted on The Creativity Assessment Platform (CAP; Patterson et al., 2025).
statements.locator: PDF p. 5, Materials and Procedure, Alternate Uses Task, scoring platform; markdown line 79

statements.quote: To account for the AI partner’s baseline creative capacity in our multilevel model, we derived a DAT score for ChatGPT-4o using an established protocol (Bellemare-Pepin et al., 2024; Cropley, 2023; Hubert et al., 2024). See SI 1 for further protocol details.
statements.locator: PDF p. 5, Materials and Procedure, Verbal Creative Thinking Ability, SI 1 reference; markdown line 83

statements.quote: Pre-registered analyses focused on originality and diversity.
statements.locator: PDF p. 7, Data Analysis, Creative Short Story Task, preregistered analyses; markdown line 109

statements.quote: Further methods description can be found in Luchini et al., 2025.
statements.locator: PDF p. 7, Data Analysis, Creative Short Story Task, reference to further methods; markdown line 109

statements.quote: See SI 2 for further analysis details.
statements.locator: PDF p. 7, Data Analysis, Creative Short Story Task, SI 2 reference; markdown line 109

statements.quote: The pre-registered model (with random slopes for condition by groupID and random intercepts for groupID and groupID:ResponseId) failed to converge, even after uncorrelating random effects.
statements.locator: PDF p. 9, Results, Alternate Uses Task, Originality, preregistered model; markdown line 168

statements.quote: Importantly, this effect was the opposite of the pre-registered analysis.
statements.locator: PDF p. 10, Results, Alternate Uses Task, Originality, human-only analysis; markdown line 209

statements.quote: Thus, contrary to the pre-registered findings, human collaborators were linked to higher originality when AI-generated responses were excluded, implying that AI responses may have previously masked underlying differences in human responses (see Fig. 2).
statements.locator: PDF p. 10, Results, Alternate Uses Task, Originality, preregistered comparison; markdown line 211

statements.quote: As indicated in the pre-registration, the linear mixed-effects model that examined elaboration (word count) with condition, participant role, and scaled DAT score as predictors initially failed to converge due to a gradient issue.
statements.locator: PDF p. 12, Results, Alternate Uses Task, Elaboration, preregistration reference; markdown line 249

statements.quote: Following the model indicated in the pre-registration, a linear mixed-effects model was conducted to examine the effects of condition and participant role on originality, controlling for scaled DAT and accounting for random effects of group ID.
statements.locator: PDF p. 14, Results, Creative Short Story Task, Originality, preregistration reference; markdown line 300

statements.quote: As indicated in the pre-registration, a separate linear mixed-effects model was conducted to examine elaboration (word count), operationalized as story word count, with condition and participant role as predictors, controlling for scaled DAT and accounting for random effects of group ID.
statements.locator: PDF p. 16, Results, Creative Short Story Task, Elaboration, preregistration reference; markdown line 326

statements.quote: We would like to acknowledge the assistance of Jimmy Pronchick, lab manager at the CNCL, for the human-AI platform.
statements.locator: PDF p. 19, Acknowledgements, human-AI platform; markdown line 384

deposits.notes: Public preregistration titled Comparing human and generative AI as collaborator in creative tasks, registered 2024-11-15. The registration contains its protocol and planned analyses as structured web/API responses, not uploaded data files. https://osf.io/tveaf returned HTTP 200. https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/tveaf/ and https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/tveaf/children/ returned HTTP 404 because this identifier is a registration; https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/tveaf/files/osfstorage/ returned HTTP 200 with zero files. The correct https://api.osf.io/v2/registrations/tveaf/ endpoint returned HTTP 200, public=true, embargoed=false, and has_data=false, has_analytic_code=false, has_materials=false, has_papers=false, has_supplements=false. The metadata retains a historical embargo_end_date of 2025-01-31, but access is now public. https://api.osf.io/v2/registrations/tveaf/files/ returned HTTP 200 and only the osfstorage provider. https://api.osf.io/v2/registrations/tveaf/files/osfstorage/, https://api.osf.io/v2/registrations/tveaf/children/, and https://api.osf.io/v2/registrations/tveaf/resources/ each returned HTTP 200 with total=0 and no next page. The materials_only classification refers to the preregistration text, not a deposited experimental-materials file. The false data-presence flags refer to actual participant assignments, scores, and responses; the protocol describes arms and outcome measures but contains no observed values. The license endpoint https://api.osf.io/v2/licenses/563c1cf88c5e4a3877f9e96a/ returned HTTP 200 and CC-By Attribution 4.0 International. Its registered_from relationship identifies private project 7t3xa. For final.open_items question 4, q15.question explicitly lists AUT Forward Flow and q17.question specifies a Levene test; these establish planned measures/analyses but cannot supply missing statistics.

notes: Checked 2026-10-09 using unauthenticated Python urllib requests with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1; no web search engine was used. Read the entire 531-line markdown conversion and checked relevant original PDF pages with PyMuPDF. The saved and current public version-2 PDF match exactly by SHA-256; it has 27 pages, with references on pp. 20-27 and no appended SI. The PDF contains the OSF preregistration link and references to supplementary information, SI 1, and SI 2, but no data-sharing/on-request statement and no data/code repository link. The form data_and_code contains empty data_url and code_url strings. The decisive availability evidence is outside the PDF: the author-supplied PsyArXiv metadata for both versions states exactly "Data made available upon request" (why_no_data). Thus status is on_request, even though a public preregistration exists and the associated project is private. No public participant-level or participant-linked output dataset was found or read. Consequently no missing per-person arm means, SDs, SEs, analyzed counts, or text-based diversity statistics can be computed from a confirmed public deposit. In particular, the public materials cannot supply the unadjusted human-only estimates (open question 2), resolve the AUT forward-flow coefficient/SE discrepancies (3), identify model-specific participant counts and exclusions (8), establish observed story-model rows (9), recover DAT arm SDs/SEs/counts (10), calculate condition-level story diversity (13), or recover the implemented allocation/matching mechanism (15). The public preregistration does help with planned-analysis status in question 4, as detailed in the preregistration notes, but this is not a computable missing statistic. Repository query bases were https://api.datacite.org/dois?query=, https://zenodo.org/api/records?q=, https://dataverse.harvard.edu/api/search?q=, and https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/?filter[title]=; query values are recorded exactly in searches. Two bibliographic OSF links related to methods/materials were also checked: https://doi.org/10.31234/osf.io/xm2f5_v2 and https://doi.org/10.31234/osf.io/zeyh3_v2 both returned HTTP 200, as did their OSF preprint API records. They identify the separate Luchini et al. story-writing study and the CAP scoring-platform paper, respectively; their data links are not evidence of a c158 deposit and are not counted. The cited Big Five Inventory-10 instrument URL https://doi.org/10.1037/t01744-000 returned HTTP 403; this is a third-party questionnaire reference, not c158 participant data, and no access bypass was attempted. The three deposit entries document the public preregistration, its private linked project, and the public preprint record carrying the on-request statement. No authors were contacted, no account was used or created, no access was requested, and no downloaded data were saved.
